correctness.rationale: For d≥2 and 0<c<1, the axial tips and transverse equator force the semiaxes of a rotational containing ellipsoid to be at least A=1−c and B=√(1−c²). The radial squared surplus of E(A,B) is 2cx(1−x/A) at 0≤x≤A. The proposed inner John ellipsoid satisfies the lens constraint with equality only at normalized axial latitudes ±1/√d; equal weights on signs and transverse signed coordinate directions give second moment I/d and zero first moment, a finite John certificate also in d=2. For the global distance, central symmetry removes translations and averaging squared shape matrices preserves both containments: the inner support constraint is linear and xᵀQ⁻¹x is a supremum of affine functions of Q. Any resulting rotational sandwich with ratio λ must contain λ⁻¹E(A,B) on its inner side. The maximum of the lens constraint on tE(A,B) for t≥1/2 is c²+t²(1−c²)+c(1−c)/2, giving t=τ=√[(2+c)/(2(1+c))] at the optimum and a matching sandwich. Its inner normalized latitude is 1/(2τ), incompatible with the John latitude because 4τ² lies strictly between 3 and 4. This checks the global optimum without assuming uniqueness of the distance ellipsoid. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; the proof, not the finite samples, establishes the result.
